results.author: Nick
results.content: Zach Cregger takes Capcom's zombie-outbreak survival horror and does exactly what a video game adaptation should do: capture the *feeling* of the games instead of slavishly recreating cutscenes. Rather than shoehorning in Leon or Claire, he builds an original story around Bryan (Austin Abrams), a hapless medical courier who stumbles into an outbreak near Raccoon City — and it works because Cregger clearly loves this world rather than just licensing it. The tense, blood-soaked gore is offset by moments of levity and humor, that signature Cregger tonal whiplash from Barbarian and Weapons — genuinely unsettling dread punctuated by "what the fuck" comedic beats that shouldn't work together but do. It's easily the best live-action Resident Evil yet. Only real complaint: the ending. Hard swerve that undercuts the tension built for two hours. Docking half a star for that alone — everything before it is a near-perfect survival horror movie.

RE? NO, a generic comedy horror.

 It's really hard to accept that 'comedy horror' genre is a thing, like this one. 

A Uber courier (with no car) sets out to make a delivery-sparking uproarious laughter in what looks like a festival of stupidity-and ends up dead. 

RE (game saga) centers on an imminent pathological outbreak that triggers a massive socio-economic transformation of society. A group attempts to expose the details regarding the responsible corporation-which defends itself by weaponizing the outbreak-thereby unleashing an exodus and a struggle for survival of the fittest. 

This movie has nothing about that, just a generic pandemic BS from a messenger perspective.

results.author: TheFilmCritics.org
results.content:
The best kind of survival horror knows that darkness is not merely a lack of light—it is a promise that something is waiting just beyond it. That instinct serves *Resident Evil* remarkably well, delivering a film that finally understands the eerie isolation and creeping dread that made the games so enduring.

The atmosphere is easily one of the movie's greatest strengths. Dark corridors, quiet stretches and an almost oppressive sense of isolation give the film the texture of survival horror rather than generic creature-feature action. The story's emphasis on being alone and cut off from safety captures the essence of the games, often making the viewer feel as though they are navigating the next room alongside the protagonist.

That commitment to suspense pays off. The film knows when to hold back and when to strike, and its jump scares are generally effective because they are built around genuine tension rather than simply being loud interruptions. There is a satisfying uncertainty to many sequences, with the audience constantly wondering what might emerge next.

The movie's original story may divide longtime fans, particularly those expecting a more direct adaptation of established Resident Evil lore. Yet setting an original narrative alongside the events of the games proves to be a sensible way to reboot the franchise. After so many previous films, a clean entry point for newcomers feels overdue. More importantly, the filmmakers clearly understand the source material: the weapons, video-game-like level structure, expendable side characters and various franchise tie-ins all feel deliberately designed rather than randomly inserted.

The practical effects are another highlight. The blood, gore and grotesque creature work have a convincing physicality that makes the horror considerably more satisfying. Unfortunately, the CGI is less consistent. Some effects blend reasonably well, while others are conspicuously digital, creating an uneven visual experience. The monsters themselves also suffer from the film's eagerness to showcase them. Their progression can feel suspiciously convenient, while some creatures are dispatched almost as quickly as they are introduced. At times, it resembles a monster highlight reel instead of allowing individual threats to develop into memorable encounters.

Pacing is sometimes inconsistent. Certain scenes rush through moments that deserved more room to breathe and build suspense, while others linger when the story clearly needs to move forward. The subplot involving the protagonist's girlfriend is particularly frustrating because it ultimately is inconsequential. There are also moments when the protagonist's goofy, humorous behavior clashes with the seriousness or urgency of the situation, making his overall tone sometimes feel inappropriate.

The ending may leave some viewers wanting more, although expectations matter here. *Resident Evil* has never been primarily about delivering profound narrative closure; audiences come for the monsters, scares, tension and grisly spectacle. On those terms, the film generally delivers. Viewers unfamiliar with the games will also miss some of the more specific references, but that does not prevent the movie from functioning as an accessible horror story in its own right.

Considering the franchise's uneven cinematic history, this *Resident Evil* is an effective return to its survival-horror roots with a story that deserves being told. It is not without rough edges, but the atmosphere, suspense, practical effects and understanding of what makes the games work give it a distinct identity. The movie is an imperfect but genuinely entertaining reboot that truly captures the essence of *Resident Evil* rather than feeling like it only wears the name.

results.author: CinemaSerf
results.content: Courier "Bryan" (Austin Abrams) is charged with delivering a vital organ through snowy conditions to a distant city hospital whilst arguing with his girlfriend on the phone about what to do about her recently discovered pregnancy. Next thing, he's clouted a woman wandering the woods at night with his car, and that's just the start of things going perilously wrong for this young man as she appears to have certain traits of lithe and nimble immortality and - well maybe she isn't alone? Abrams holds this together really quite well, and his dead pan delivery is really pretty engaging. Sure, the plot itself isn't that original and it's not really so similar to the 2002 version, but the wintry conditions set the scene darkly and a little claustrophobically and there's some fun to be had from a dialogue that tells us amidsts all his perils, that his socks are wet! The visual effects used to conjure up his nemesis are used sparingly but still quite effectively and the traditionally accumulating elements of the video game shoot'-em-up that we find here are actually acknowledged as part of the humour. The ending wasn't my favourite - it has something of the gory slapstick to it and maybe suggests a sequel, but Abrams holds the film together entertainingly by characterising his "Bryan" as an adaptable and cheeky character that - unusually for me - I actually did want to root for rather than see gobbled up by any monster. It's really hard to be fresh with this genre - same old, same old, week in, week out - but this spent more time on the writing and on a lead actor who leaves out the histrionics and brings us something that's really quite good fun.

results.author: Sierbahnn
results.content: As a adaptation of the Resident Evil franchise, this is really, really good. It beats the last movie, Welcome to Raccoon City, and is far more in line with the feeling of playing a Resident Evil game. The main protagonist isn't a skilled operative or military, he's just a guy who happens to get tangled up in extraordinarily gory and scary circumstances. He therefore acts accordingly. He struggles with things that action heroes take for granted, and it makes him far more interesting to watch than the protagonists of the last movie, for instance. The effect work is, of course, superb, as it would need to be in a movie like this, and it is a fun time overall. I recommend this wholeheartedly.

results.author: Manuel São Bento
results.content:
Check out my full review @ https://www.manuelsbento.com/resident-evil-2026-zach-cregger-turns-a-beloved-franchise-into-the-horror-comedy-of-the-year/

Rating: B

I went into RESIDENT EVIL having never played or watched a single entry in this franchise, and I still had a blast. Zach Cregger turns a video game he clearly loves into a horror-comedy that's relentlessly gory, genuinely funny, and stuffed with jump scares that actually worked on me. It's predictable once the machinery kicks in, and it doesn't carry the thematic weight of his last two films, but as a purely fun night at the movies, this delivers exactly what it promises.

results.author: Ryan Ting
results.content: The 8th live action film of the Resident Evil series serves as a reboot by director Zach Cregger, the man behind the film, Weapons. This film plots a medical courier who must fight through an outbreak of infected monsters in a fictional town of Raccoon City. Ultimately, at the end of the movie, he becomes fully infected & killed the last scientist, causing the cure to fall from the rooftop.

results.author: kevinzhang87
results.content:
Resident Evil 2026 discards survival horror to deliver an relentless comedy special masquerading as an apocalyptic outbreak. Director Zach Cregger trades genuine dread for punchlines, turning bio-weapon chaos into an arena for cynical, rapid-fire banter.

Instead of claustrophobic tension, characters treat flesh-eating abominations like mild annoyances, tossing off mean-spirited quips faster than spent shotgun shells. While die-hard franchise purists seeking atmospheric dread will end up disappointed, fans of black comedy will relish the absurdity. It’s brutal, deeply sarcastic, and utterly uninterested in scaring you.

In short, this is not a Resident Evil movie. This is a stand-up show packed with cynical gags.

results.author: Dean
results.content: This isn't a typical Resident Evil movie. It's different, however it's not bad. It's a dark comedy. I usually don't like comedy genre, but I liked this one. The cast feels like real people caught in a nightmare rather than indestructible action heroes.

results.author: Chris Sawin
results.content:
The cool thing about this adaptation of Resident Evil is that it caters to both longtime fans of the video game franchise and movie lovers looking for something entertaining. The film utilizes what made the games so entertaining and memorable, but it revolves around a unique story with original characters. Meanwhile, the film is horror on the surface, but it's also quite funny, has a lot of action, and is incredibly thrilling. It utilizes several genres to entertain the audience, making the film a fantastic crowd-pleaser.

results.title: Die Alone
results.overview: Lost in a world reclaimed by nature and overrun by mysterious creatures, Ethan, a young man with amnesia navigates the dangerous landscape in search of his lost love Emma.  His journey takes an unexpected turn when he encounters Mae, a hardened and eccentric survivor.  Together, Ethan and Mae face threats both human and otherwise before a fateful encounter with Kai unravels a secret that lies just beyond Ethan's fractured memory.

results.title: Land of the Dead
results.overview: The living dead have taken over the world, and the remaining humans live in a walled city to protect themselves as they cope with the situation.

results.title: Resident Evil
results.overview: When a virus leaks from a top-secret facility, turning all resident researchers into ravenous zombies and their lab animals into mutated hounds from hell, the government sends in an elite military task force to contain the outbreak.

results.title: Resident Evil: Extinction
results.overview: Years after the Racoon City catastrophe, survivors travel across the Nevada desert, hoping to make it to Alaska. Alice joins the caravan and their fight against hordes of zombies and the evil Umbrella Corp.

results.title: Re-Kill
results.overview: Five years after a zombie outbreak, the men and women of R-Division hunt down and destroy the undead. When they see signs of a second outbreak, they fear humanity may not survive.

results.title: Resident Evil: Apocalypse
results.overview: As the city is locked down under quarantine, Alice finds out that the people that died from the previous incident at the Umbrella Corporation have turned into zombies. She then joins a small band of elite soldiers, who are enlisted to rescue the missing daughter of the creator of the mutating T-virus.  Once lack of luck and resources happen, they begin to wage an exhilarating battle to survive and escape before the Umbrella Corporation erases its experiment from the face of the earth.

results.title: Extinction
results.overview: And suddenly, overnight, the world came to a halt. Two men, two survivors, one kid, and hatred that separates them. A place forgotten by everyone, including the creatures that inhabit the Earth... until now.

results.title: Dawn of the Dead
results.overview: A group of survivors take refuge in a shopping mall after the world is taken over by aggressive, flesh-eating zombies.

results.title: Year 10
results.overview: After the fall of civilization, the few survivors have been driven to cannibalism. A young man must confront a violent tribe that has murdered his father and stolen the medicine that keeps his girlfriend alive.

results.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
results.overview: An apocalyptic story set in the furthest reaches of our planet, in a stark desert landscape where humanity is broken, and most everyone is crazed fighting for the necessities of life. Within this world exist two rebels on the run who just might be able to restore order.

results.title: The Resurrected
results.overview: Charles Dexter Ward, a wealthy scientist, uses an ancient diary and human remains to begin a terrifying and bloody pursuit for immortality.

results.title: Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City
results.original_title: Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City
results.overview: Once the booming home of pharmaceutical giant Umbrella Corporation, Raccoon City is now a dying Midwestern town. The company’s exodus left the city a wasteland…with great evil brewing below the surface. When that evil is unleashed, the townspeople are forever…changed…and a small group of survivors must work together to uncover the truth behind Umbrella and make it through the night.

results.title: 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple
results.overview: Dr. Kelson finds himself in a shocking new relationship - with consequences that could change the world as they know it - and Spike's encounter with Jimmy Crystal becomes a nightmare he can't escape.

results.title: Daylight's End
results.overview: Years after a mysterious plague has devastated the planet and turned most of humanity into blood-hungry creatures, a rogue drifter on a vengeful hunt stumbles across a band of survivors in an abandoned police station and reluctantly agrees to try to help them defend themselves and escape to the sanctuary they so desperately need.

results.title: Lifeforce
results.overview: A race of space vampires arrives in London and infects the populace, commencing an apocalyptic descent into chaos.

results.title: World War Z
results.overview: Life for former United Nations investigator Gerry Lane and his family seems content. Suddenly, the world is plagued by a mysterious infection turning whole human populations into rampaging mindless zombies. After barely escaping the chaos, Lane is persuaded to go on a mission to investigate this disease. What follows is a perilous trek around the world where Lane must brave horrific dangers and long odds to find answers before human civilization falls.

results.title: 28 Years Later
results.overview: Twenty-eight years after the Rage virus outbreak, a heavily-defended island survives connected to the mainland by a single causeway. When one of the group leaves the island into the dark heart of the mainland, he discovers secrets, wonders, and horrors that have mutated not only the infected but other survivors as well.

results.title: Primitive War
results.overview: During the Vietnam War, a recon unit ventures to an isolated jungle valley to uncover the fate of a missing platoon. They soon find themselves in a fight for their lives against an unexpected enemy — prehistoric dinosaurs.

results.title: Tremors: A Cold Day in Hell
results.original_title: Tremors: A Cold Day in Hell
results.overview: Burt Gummer and Travis Welker find themselves in a fight for survival after investigating deadly giant worm attacks in the Canadian arctic.

results.title: Monster Hunters
results.overview: When an alien prison ship crash lands and unleashes creature after creature in the California desert, they make quick work of the army that tries to stop them. Now, the only hope of stopping the aliens rests with a secret branch of the government specializing in alien weaponry. But with the team untested in actual combat, the battle for Earth will be brutal.
